_readme: P1 recurring people and their offscreen lives (decided 2026-10-02; master handoff §11). Each person has a goal, a vulnerability, people they care about, someone they distrust, a household, status, an opinion, an outside interest and a voice. Their lives go on without the player: each 'life' entry can happen once, from 'fromMonth' (months since AD 155-01), once its 'requires' all hold, with 'chance' each month (seeded). Requirements: commission:<id>:<status>, access:<institution>:<stage or later>, capability:<id>:<level or later>, life:<id>. Effects: 'awayMonths' (the person can't invite or introduce anyone), 'status' per person, 'capability' with 'spread' (imitation: Local / Copied / Widespread, optionally 'distorted' and 'misattributed'; it never raises true maturity) or 'to' (a true advance the person makes themselves). 'interrupt' marks a world interruption that bypasses the scene router. No inevitability (Corey, 2026-10-04): 'windowMonths' bounds how long after it first becomes possible an event can happen, 'decay' lowers the monthly chance each month it has been possible, 'group' makes branches mutually exclusive, 'leaves' takes the person out of Rome for good. 'known' says when the player knows them; 'echoes' are what the inventor may find of them on an arrival: each line at most once, 'fromJump' (default 1) the first arrival it can appear on, later arrivals preferring their own lines (aged consequences, descendants, deaths, contradictory memory); at most echoes.peoplePerArrival people an arrival. Chances PROPOSED P1-08.

people.name: Felix
people.role: a freedman who fits out ships at Ostia and in Rome, and a member of the guild
people.goal: to be the man two shops send for when they can't agree
people.vulnerability: the marsh fever from Ostia, which comes back most years
people.caresAbout: his wife Prima and the two boys he is putting through a grammarian
people.distrusts: the shippers who pay late and the guild's older families, who still call him a freedman
people.household: a wife, two sons, a slave-born clerk he freed last year
people.status: known on the quays; a member of the guild, not yet an officer
people.opinion: a good fitting is worth more than a clever one
people.interest: the Blues at the Circus, loudly
people.voice: quick, warm, always halfway to the next errand

echoes.text: In the guild hall at Ostia the old contracts on the wall have one witness over and over: Felix. The fitters call him Felix who connected the shops. One says he once sponsored a foreign craftsman; no one remembers the name.
On the quays at Ostia a ship-fitter's yard has FELICIS cut over the gate. His grandsons run it, and argue about the Blues.

The guild at Ostia keeps a feast for its founders now. Felix is on the list, though he founded nothing; the speech calls him the man who taught the shops to trust each other's measures. An apprentice tells you the foreigner Felix sponsored was really a Greek from Alexandria.

FELICIS is still cut over the yard gate at Ostia, but the yard makes rope now. The family sold the fitting trade after two brothers quarrelled; one went to Puteoli and did well, the other stayed and didn't.

people.name: Cassianus
people.role: a grain and oil merchant with warehouses under the Aventine
people.goal: to keep his oil dry and his name good with the Ostia shippers
people.vulnerability: everything he owns sits in one row of warehouses
people.distrusts: the neighbour across the lane, Pollio, who undersells him
people.household: a widowed sister who keeps his accounts, a daughter, porters
people.status: comfortable, and worried about staying so
people.opinion: a foreigner who fixes things is worth knowing, and worth watching
people.voice: careful, counts aloud, repeats a price back to make sure

echoes.text: The warehouses under the Aventine were rebuilt in brick after a fire, long ago. The cellar under the third one is still dry.
Cassianus's warehouses under the Aventine belong to his daughter's family now. The cellar is dry.
A stone in the lane under the Aventine settles an old lawsuit: the heirs of Cassianus and of Pollio share a wall and a well by the praetor's order. The two families still don't marry.
The third warehouse under the Aventine is a bathhouse now. The owner shows you the old pump in the cellar, green with age, and says a foreigner built it for his great-grandfather from Hero's books.

people.name: Diodoros
people.goal: more responsibility and more pay than carrying jars
people.vulnerability: his back and his hands are his living
people.caresAbout: a mother in Antioch he sends money to
people.distrusts: the overseer who docks his pay
people.household: a room above a bakery with two other porters
people.opinion: the men who know how a thing works are never the ones paid for it
people.voice: few words, Greek when he is angry

echoes.text: A cloth merchant from Antioch, in Rome to sell, asks if you knew a porter called Diodoros. His father worked for him, he says: a one-handed man who could fix any pump on the Orontes, and told everyone he learned it in Rome.
A carters' yard by the Porta Trigemina belongs to a family from Antioch. The man who started it, they say, could only use one hand.

The carters' yard by the Porta Trigemina has become three yards and a feud. Diodoros's tombstone stands in the oldest one: a man with one hand raised, a citizen of Antioch and of Rome, it says, though he was never a citizen of either.

people.name: Titus Aelius Serenus
people.role: a physician of the Subura, a member of the Physicians' Circle
people.goal: to show that a physician can know which treatment works, not just argue for one
people.vulnerability: his patients are poor and his fees are small; the Circle's grander men look down on him
people.caresAbout: a sister in the Subura who keeps his house and his casebooks
people.distrusts: physicians who treat by the stars and charge by the hour
people.household: his sister, a freedman who grinds his drugs, and a cat that sleeps on the casebooks
people.status: a member of the Circle, not one of its leading men
people.opinion: Galen is brilliant and talks too much
people.voice: blunt, short sentences, a joke when you least expect one

echoes.text: In the Circle's library a casebook in a careful hand sits chained to the shelf: Serenus's fevers, set side by side, with notes in three later hands arguing with him.
A physician quotes Serenus's fevers at you to prove a point Serenus would have hated. The casebooks have been copied so often that half the cases in them never happened.

people.name: Gaius Fabius Crispus
people.role: a bronze worker with a shop on the Clivus, the one who first cut seats to your foot
people.goal: for his shop to be the one other shops copy, not the one that copies
people.vulnerability: pride: he would rather lose a month than be told how to hold a file
people.caresAbout: Livia, their two daughters, and his sister's boy Marcus
people.distrusts: Priscus, the bigger bronze shop by the river, which hires away anyone good
people.household: Livia, two daughters, his nephew Marcus at the bench, an old slave who keeps the furnace
people.status: a master with three men and a reputation on the Clivus
people.opinion: a tool you can't mend yourself is a debt
people.interest: the Greens, though he says it's only for Livia's sake
people.voice: slow, dry, says no first and maybe later

echoes.text: On the Clivus a shop with a water-driven grinder in the yard has CRISPI over the door. The men inside argue about whose grandfather built the shaft.

The Fabian works by the river are a dozen sheds now, all on one race. A carved relief over the gate shows a bronze worker at a lathe and a woman holding a green ribbon; nobody there knows who she was.

people.name: Livia
people.role: Gaius's wife, who runs the household and half the shop's accounts
people.goal: daughters well married and a shop that doesn't eat the family
people.vulnerability: the family's money is all in the shop
people.caresAbout: her daughters, and Gaius more than she lets him see
people.distrusts: men who promise her husband glory
people.status: a craftsman's wife, sharp, known on the street
people.opinion: the Greens will win when the Blues run out of bribes
people.interest: the Circus, the Greens, and every piece of gossip on the Clivus
people.voice: teasing, quick, never says the serious thing straight

people.name: Marcus Fabius Tertius
people.role: Gaius's sister's son, at the bench in Gaius's shop
people.goal: a shop of his own, the one his father the clerk never got
people.vulnerability: his pride; he hears every correction as a judgment of his father
people.caresAbout: his widowed mother, and being taken seriously
people.distrusts: his uncle's caution, which he calls fear
people.household: his mother, in two rooms above a cookshop
people.status: an apprentice who thinks he should be a journeyman
people.opinion: a man who writes things down is a clerk, and he will not be a clerk
people.voice: eager, defensive, finishes other people's sentences wrong

people.name: Lucan
people.role: an old smith near the Porta Trigemina who taught half the smiths on the river
people.goal: to see one of his apprentices do better than him
people.caresAbout: the craft, and a granddaughter who sells eggs
people.distrusts: anyone who can draw a thing but not make it
people.household: a granddaughter and too many cats
people.interest: the old soldiers' stories at the tavern

people.name: Aulus Septimius Crispus
people.role: a millwright who keeps the mills on the Janiculum turning
people.goal: mills that run all year without him being called out at night
people.vulnerability: his back, from forty years of lifting stones and shafts
people.caresAbout: his sons, both millwrights at Ostia
people.distrusts: anyone who adds a part a man can't reach to grease
people.household: a wife who sells bread from the mill, two grown sons
people.status: a craftsman every mill owner on the hill knows
people.opinion: water does the work; men only spoil it
people.voice: short orders, concrete, never explains twice

people.name: Sextus Nerius
people.role: owner of a finishing shop where twelve men polish and fit bronze by hand
people.goal: to keep his shop and his men, and to be paid what the work is worth
people.vulnerability: his men are his shop; without them he is a room
people.caresAbout: his men, some of whom have been with him twenty years
people.household: a wife, a son who wants to be a lawyer
people.status: a solid man of the trades
people.opinion: good finishing is done by hand, or it isn't good
people.interest: his son's speeches, which he pretends to understand
people.voice: plain, worried, asks the same question twice in different words

life.text: Prima sends a boy: the marsh fever has Felix again. No suppers and no quays for him for a month or two.
life.returnText: Felix is back on the quays, thinner, asking after your work before his own.

status.Cassianus: rebuilding after the fire; he lost a season's oil
status.Diodoros: his right hand burned in the fire; he can't carry

life.text: Fire in the warehouses under the Aventine in the night. Cassianus loses a season's oil. His porter Diodoros burns his hand dragging jars out of the smoke. Below it all, in the wet cellar, your pump still draws.

status.Diodoros: runs Cassianus's deliveries and keeps the pump, one-handed

life.text: Diodoros can't carry with that hand, so Cassianus has him run the deliveries and see to the pump. He knows its seats better than Cassianus does.

Diodoros comes to the workshop to say goodbye. A porter with one good hand is no porter, and his mother has written that his uncle needs a man in his shop in Antioch. He has his pay in a knotted cloth and a place on a grain ship back east. He shakes your hand with the left.

status.Cassianus: furious that Pollio has a pump like his

life.text: Pollio, across the lane from Cassianus, has had a pump made like his by a bronzesmith on the Clivus who saw it once. The seats are cut by eye and it leaks back on every stroke. Pollio tells everyone the design is yours.

status.Marcus: working for Priscus by the river, with an apprentice of his own

life.text: Marcus doesn't come to the bench. Livia tells you: Priscus has offered him half again Gaius's pay and a boy of his own to order about. Gaius says nothing all day and breaks a file.

status.Marcus: keeping the shaft's tally book, and still wanting a shop of his own

life.text: Priscus offers Marcus half again his pay. Marcus tells him no, then tells everyone on the Clivus he said no. He asks you to show him how to keep the tally of the shaft properly, every hour of it, as if it had been his idea.
